heading: Components
body:
Each component folder under client/components becomes a tag with hyphens: components/panel/users becomes panel-users. You pass props (the values a component receives) as attributes. The lazy attribute waits to load the component until it scrolls into view. To use a component outside your Tac app, list it in `tac.elements` (see Components in other apps).

A component shows the children that it receives in a slot. `<slot>` holds every child without a `slot` attribute. A named slot, such as `<slot name="title">`, holds the children whose `slot` attribute has that name, such as `<page-title slot="title" />`. A slot name is fixed text that is not empty (`TY1302`). A child for a slot that the component does not declare stops the build with `TY1404`, and so do children without a `slot` attribute when the component has no `<slot>`.

The markup of a component belongs in its `tac.html`, and its styles belong in its `tac.css`. A client script changes text, classes and service state, but it does not build markup or write styles (`TY1364`). The build refuses `innerHTML` and `outerHTML` writes (also with `||=`, `??=` or `+=`), `document.write`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `setHTML`, `setHTMLUnsafe`, inserting nodes made with `document.createElement`, writes to `element.style` or its fields, `setAttribute('style', ...)` and style sheet changes. It follows them through aliases, fields of objects such as `refs.list`, `bind`, `call` and `apply`. The check reads the source when you build. It checks a convention and is not a sandbox, so a computed name such as `element[name]` is not followed. A third-party script that builds its own markup is declared in `tac.scriptSources` (`TY1365`).
